## KyrolusSous.CQRS (Enterprise CQRS Pipeline)
Enterprise-grade CQRS foundation for .NET 10 with 12 ordered pipeline behaviors, outbox pattern, real-time live push, read-model projections, dynamic specifications, and generic CRUD query/command handlers for Entity Framework Core and Marten.

### Pipeline Ordering Standard

| Order | Pipeline Behavior | Description |
| :---: | :--- | :--- |
| **`-2000`** | `KyrolusExceptionMappingBehavior` | Translates domain exceptions into structured responses or problem details. |
| **`-1000`** | `KyrolusAuthorizationBehavior` | Enforces authentication, roles, permissions, scopes, and `[KyrolusAuthorize]`. |
| **`-900`** | `KyrolusPerformanceAndTelemetryBehavior` | OpenTelemetry distributed tracing spans, execution duration, and slow request warnings. |
| **`-850`** | `KyrolusAuditBehavior` | Captures audit records to `IAuditSink` with automatic sensitive credential redaction. |
| **`-800`** | `KyrolusIdempotencyBehavior` | Guarantees command deduplication via cache keys (`IIdempotentCommand`). |
| **`-750`** | `KyrolusThrottlingBehavior` | Concurrency limiting and semaphore-based backpressure per partition key. |
| **`-700`** | `KyrolusEfTransactionBehavior` / `KyrolusMartenTransactionBehavior` | Atomic database transaction boundaries and execution strategies. |
| **`-650`** | `KyrolusDomainEventsDispatchBehavior` / `KyrolusMartenDomainEventsDispatchBehavior` | Drains and dispatches entity domain events via `IKyrolusMediatorPublisher`. |
| **`-600`** | `KyrolusReadModelProjectionBehavior` | Synchronizes polyglot read models (e.g. Elasticsearch/Redis) on successful command commits. |
| **`-550`** | `KyrolusLivePushBehavior` | Real-time live update broadcasting to connected UI clients (SignalR / WebSockets). |
| **`-500`** | `KyrolusValidationBehavior` | Aggregates multi-engine validators (FluentValidation + DataAnnotations). |
| **`-300`** | `KyrolusQueryCachingBehavior` | Caches query responses with smart cache keys, pagination partitions, and tag invalidation. |

### Registration

```csharp
// Register complete CQRS pipeline
builder.Services
    .AddKyrolusCqrsAuthorization()
    .AddKyrolusCqrsAudit()
    .AddKyrolusCqrsOutbox()
    .AddKyrolusCqrsProjections()
    .AddKyrolusCqrsLivePush()
    .AddKyrolusCqrsCaching()
    .AddKyrolusCqrsValidation()
    .AddKyrolusCqrsEf<MyDbContext>()
    .AddKyrolusCqrsMarten<IDocumentSession>();
```

### Transactional Outbox Pattern

```csharp
// Store pending messages atomically within database transactions
public sealed class OrderCreatedEvent : INotification;

// Process outbox background queue
var processor = app.Services.GetRequiredService<KyrolusOutboxProcessor>();
var processedCount = await processor.ProcessPendingMessagesAsync(batchSize: 50);
```

## KyrolusSous.EndpointKit (Core + EF)
Mediator-first endpoint scaffolding for Minimal APIs. Core is framework-agnostic (Mediator abstractions only), while EF adds query/paging/filter/include support via CQRS.EF and EF query primitives.

**Packages**
- `KyrolusSous.EndpointKit.Core`
- `KyrolusSous.EndpointKit.EF` (provider package)

  **What you get**
    - CRUD endpoints out of the box (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE).
    - Per-endpoint configuration (authorization, default includes, view models).
    - Query endpoints (string filter or `QueryRequest`).
    - Paged endpoints (GET /paged, POST /query/paged).
    - Includes with dot paths (`Orders.Items`) and expression includes for simple paths.
    - Field projection via `fields` (comma list) or `QueryRequest.Fields`.
    - Composite key endpoints (`/by-keys`) for GET/PATCH/DELETE when enabled.
    - Bulk endpoints (update/delete) for large operations.
    - Allowlists + strict validation for filters/order/includes.
    - Cacheable flag propagated to CQRS (`ICacheableRequest`).
    - Per-endpoint rate limiting + idempotency (optional).
    - Versioned route prefix (e.g., `/api/v1`).

  **OpenAPI responses (from config)**
  - Default response codes are applied automatically (200/201 + 400, plus 401/403 if auth is required, and 404 for GetById).
  - Override globally with `DefaultResponses`, or per endpoint with `EndpointConfig[].Responses`.

  ```csharp
  config.DefaultResponses = new[]
  {
      new KyrolusOpenApiResponse(StatusCodes.Status200OK, typeof(ProductDto)),
      new KyrolusOpenApiResponse(StatusCodes.Status400BadRequest)
  };

  config.EndpointConfig =
  [
      new KyrolusEndpointConfig
      {
          Name = EndpointNames.GetById,
          Responses = new[]
          {
              new KyrolusOpenApiResponse(StatusCodes.Status200OK, typeof(ProductDto)),
              new KyrolusOpenApiResponse(StatusCodes.Status404NotFound)
          }
      }
  ];
  ```

### Quick start
```csharp
builder.Services.AddKyrolusDefaults(); // registers EF route mapper + default handlers

builder.Services.AddKyrolus(modules =>
{
    var config = new KyrolusEfApiConfig<Product>
    {
        ApiName = "Products",
        Route = "product",
        ViewModelType = typeof(ProductDto),
        ApiVersion = "1",
        VersionPrefix = "v",
        AppendVersionToPrefix = true,
        RateLimitPolicy = "fixed",
        EnableIdempotency = true,
        IdempotencyHeaderName = "Idempotency-Key",
        IdempotencyTtl = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10),
        QueryAll = new GetAllQuery<Product>(),
        QueryById = new GetByIdQuery<Product, Guid>(Guid.Empty),
        QueryByProperty = new GetAllQuery<Product>(),
        AddCommand = new AddCommand<Product>(default!),
        AddRangeCommand = new AddRangeCommand<Product>([]),
        UpdateCommand = new UpdateCommand<Product>(default!),
        UpdateRangeCommand = new UpdateRangeCommand<Product>([]),
        PatchCommand = new PatchCommand<Product, Guid>(null, new Dictionary<string, object>()),
        RemoveCommand = new RemoveByIdCommand<Product, Guid>(null),
        RemoveRangeCommand = new RemoveRangeCommand<Product>([]),
        ExecuteUpdateCommand = new ExecuteUpdateCommand<Product, Guid>(p => true, new Dictionary<string, object>(), false, null),
        ExecuteDeleteCommand = new ExecuteDeleteCommand<Product, Guid>(p => true, false, null),
          AllowedFilterProperties = new[] { "Name", "Price", "CategoryId" },
          AllowedOrderProperties = new[] { "Name", "Price", "CreatedAt" },
          AllowedIncludeProperties = new[] { "Category", "OrderLines", "OrderLines.Order" },
          AllowedSelectProperties = new[] { "Id", "Name", "Price", "Category.Name" },
          StrictFilterValidation = true,
          StrictIncludeValidation = true,
          StrictSelectValidation = true,
          DefaultPageSize = 50,
          MaxPageSize = 200,
          EnableCompositeKeyEndpoints = true,
          CompositeKeyOnly = true,
          CompositeKeyParser = parts => new object?[]
          {
              Guid.Parse(parts[0], CultureInfo.InvariantCulture),
              int.Parse(parts[1], CultureInfo.InvariantCulture)
          },
          CompositeKeyTypes = new[] { typeof(Guid), typeof(int) },
          EnableBulkEndpoints = true
      };

    modules.AddModule<BaseKyrolusModule<Product, ProductCreateDto, Guid>, Product, ProductCreateDto, Guid>(config);
});

app.MapKyrolus();
```

### Endpoints generated (Core + EF)
- `GET /{route}s`  
  Query params: `filter`, `includedProps`, `fields`, `cacheable`
- `GET /{route}/{id}`  
  Query params: `includedProps`, `fields`, `cacheable`
- `POST /{route}` (Create)
- `POST /{route}s` (CreateRange)
- `PUT /{route}/{id}` (Update)
- `PATCH /{route}/{id}` (Patch)
- `PUT /{route}s` (UpdateRange)
- `DELETE /{route}/{id}` (Delete)
- `DELETE /{route}s` (DeleteRange)
- `GET /{route}/by-keys`  
  Query params: `keys`, `includedProps`, `fields`, `cacheable`
- `PATCH /{route}/by-keys`  
  Query params: `keys`, `cacheable`
- `DELETE /{route}/by-keys`  
  Query params: `keys`, `cacheable`
- `POST /{route}s/query`  
  Body: `QueryRequest`
- `GET /{route}s/paged`  
  Query params: `filter`, `orderBy`, `includes`, `fields`, `pageNumber`, `pageSize`, `cacheable`, `asNoTracking`, `useSplitQuery`
- `POST /{route}s/query/paged`  
  Body: `KyrolusEfPagedQueryRequest`
- `GET /{route}s/export`  
  Query params: `filter`, `includedProps`, `fields`, `format` (e.g. `format=csv`)
- `POST /{route}s/bulk/update`  
  Body: `KyrolusEfBulkUpdateRequest`
- `POST /{route}s/bulk/delete`  
  Body: `KyrolusEfBulkDeleteRequest`

### Endpoint Filters & Exporters
- **`KyrolusValidationEndpointFilter`**: ASP.NET Core `IEndpointFilter` that runs `IKyrolusValidationEngine` on request DTOs and emits standardized `ProblemDetails` via `KyrolusSous.ExceptionHandling` without duplicate code.
- **`KyrolusTelemetryEndpointFilter`**: Enriches OpenTelemetry `Activity.Current` with `endpointkit.entity`, `endpointkit.action`, and route tags.
- **`KyrolusCsvExporter`**: High-throughput, invariant-culture CSV streaming exporter for zero-allocation data downloads.

### Bulk update/delete
```http
POST /api/product/bulk/update
```
```json
{
  "request": {
    "filters": [
      { "property": "Price", "operator": "lt", "value": "50" }
    ],
    "useSplitQuery": false
  },
  "updates": {
    "Price": 55.5,
    "IsActive": true
  },
  "cacheable": false
}
```

```http
POST /api/product/bulk/delete
```
```json
{
  "request": {
    "filters": [
      { "property": "IsDeleted", "operator": "eq", "value": "true" }
    ]
  },
  "cacheable": false
}
```

### String filter syntax (GET /{route}s)
- AND: comma `,`  
- OR: pipe `|`
- Example: `Name==John,Price>=100|CategoryId==1`

### QueryRequest (POST /{route}s/query)
```json
{
  "includes": ["Category", "OrderLines.Order"],
  "fields": ["Id", "Name", "Category.Name"],
  "orderBy": [{ "property": "CreatedAt", "desc": true }],
  "filters": [
    { "property": "Name", "operator": "contains", "value": "soft" },
    { "property": "Price", "operator": "gte", "value": "100" }
  ],
  "asNoTracking": true,
  "useSplitQuery": true
}
```

### Field selection (projection)
```http
GET /api/product?fields=Id,Name,Category.Name
```

### Composite key endpoints
`keys` accepts repeated values (`keys=...&keys=...`) or a single comma list (`keys=a,b`).
You can enable typed conversion via `CompositeKeyTypes` or a custom `CompositeKeyParser`.
Set `CompositeKeyOnly = true` to disable `/id` endpoints and expose only `/by-keys` for GET/PATCH/DELETE.

```http
GET    /api/orderline/by-keys?keys=8d5f1b5b-0baf-4b5c-8a8b-0a59b4d6d7a1&keys=12
PATCH  /api/orderline/by-keys?keys=8d5f1b5b-0baf-4b5c-8a8b-0a59b4d6d7a1,12
DELETE /api/orderline/by-keys?keys=8d5f1b5b-0baf-4b5c-8a8b-0a59b4d6d7a1&keys=12
```

### Rate limiting + idempotency
```csharp
config.RateLimitPolicy = "fixed"; // registered ASP.NET RateLimiter policy
config.EnableIdempotency = true;
config.IdempotencyHeaderName = "Idempotency-Key";
config.IdempotencyTtl = TimeSpan.FromMinutes(10);
```

Example request:
```http
POST /api/product
Idempotency-Key: 0f9f7b2b-7d36-4f4b-9d4f-0b6d9fd1ab4c
```

### Versioned routes
```csharp
config.ApiVersion = "1";
config.VersionPrefix = "v";
config.AppendVersionToPrefix = true;
// Result: /api/v1/{route}s
```

### Includes
- Simple includes are converted to expression includes for performance.
- Dot paths (`Orders.Items`) are kept as string includes.

### View models
You can return different view models per endpoint:
```csharp
public sealed class EndpointConfig : IEndpointConfig
{
    public EndpointNames Name { get; set; }
    public string[] IncludeProps { get; set; } = [];
    public Type? ViewModelType { get; set; }
    public bool Authorize { get; set; }
    public dynamic? AuthorizationPolicy { get; set; }
}

config.EndpointConfig = new[]
{
    new EndpointConfig
    {
        Name = EndpointNames.GetAll,
        ViewModelType = typeof(ProductListDto),
        IncludeProps = ["Category"],
        Authorize = true,
        AuthorizationPolicy = "Products.Read"
    }
};
```

### Replace mapping
The mapping subsystem is powered by `KyrolusSous.Mapping`. Register `IKyrolusObjectMapper` via `services.AddKyrolusMapping()`.

## KyrolusSous.Auth (Abstractions + Runtime + OpenIddict + 8 providers)

Sign-in for an ASP.NET Core application: eight external identity providers, an OpenIddict
authorization server, and the four protocol endpoints most projects otherwise write by hand.

**Not tied to any ORM or database.** The whole family talks to storage through exactly one
interface, `IKyrolusAuthUserStore`. Implement it over EF Core, Marten, Dapper, MongoDB, an
in-memory list or a remote user service - none of these packages knows or cares which. There is
no `DbContext`, no entity base class, no migration to run.

| Package | What it gives you |
| --- | --- |
| `KyrolusSous.Auth.Abstractions` | Storage-agnostic contracts: the user model, store, password hasher, claims-principal factory, external-login hook, and lockout abstractions. |
| `KyrolusSous.Auth.Runtime` | Default implementations: PBKDF2 hashing, claims factory, external-login provisioning, user authenticator, and an in-memory store. |
| `KyrolusSous.Auth.OpenIddict` | OIDC authorization server and resource server configuration, claim destinations, and ready-made `/connect/*` endpoints. |
| `KyrolusSous.Auth.Jwt` | Lightweight, high-performance JWT access & refresh token generator and non-blocking token validator with 8KB size bounds. |
| `KyrolusSous.Auth.ApiKey` | API key authentication handler, cryptographically secure key generator, SHA-256 validator, and header pollution protection. |
| `KyrolusSous.Auth.Mfa` | RFC 6238 TOTP engine, Base32 encoder/decoder, QR code URI generator, and secure recovery code service with 80-bit entropy. |
| `KyrolusSous.Auth.Security` | Brute-force lockout guard with sliding window, automatic eviction, and NIST SP 800-63B password policy checker. |
| `KyrolusSous.Auth.MagicLink` | Passwordless authentication service, atomic single-use token consumption, HMAC-SHA256 store, and HTTP/HTTPS redirect scheme validation. |
| `KyrolusSous.Auth.Sessions` | Device session manager, heartbeat telemetry, remote revocation, user-agent sanitization, and concurrent session eviction. |
| `KyrolusSous.Auth.TokenRevocation` | Distributed token blacklist, JTI tracking, Unix epoch sub-second alignment, and cutoff revocation validator. |
| `KyrolusSous.Auth.Permissions` | RBAC and fine-grained permission authorization handler, wildcard matching, hierarchical evaluation, and endpoint filter. |
| `KyrolusSous.Auth.MultiTenancy` | Multi-tenant resolution pipeline: HTTP headers, JWT claims, subdomains, and composite failover with ASCII homoglyph protection. |
| `KyrolusSous.Auth.Events` | Security audit event pipeline: user login, failed attempts, lockouts, token revocations, and fault-tolerant dispatcher. |
| `KyrolusSous.Auth.Impersonation` | Administrator user impersonation service with actor claims, duration expiry, tenant preservation, and nested impersonation blocking. |
| `KyrolusSous.Auth.Tokens` | HMAC-SHA256 user tokens for email confirmation and password reset with delimiter escaping and clock-skew tolerance. |
| `KyrolusSous.Auth.EntityFramework` | Optional companion storage adapter for EF Core with idempotent external login and lockout persistence. |
| `KyrolusSous.Auth.Marten` | Optional companion storage adapter for Marten document store with query normalization and lockout persistence. |
| `KyrolusSous.Auth.Google` `.MicrosoftAccount` `.Apple` `.Facebook` `.GitHub` `.X` `.LinkedIn` `.Discord` | External OAuth 2.0 social identity providers with unified options and startup validation. |

### External login

```csharp
services.AddKyrolusGoogleAuth(options =>
{
    options.ClientId = configuration["Auth:Google:ClientId"]!;
    options.ClientSecret = configuration["Auth:Google:ClientSecret"]!;
    options.AutoCreateUser = true;               // provision on first sign-in
    options.LinkToExistingUserByEmail = true;    // only ever on a verified email
});

services.AddKyrolusAuthCore();                   // hasher, sign-in policy, claims factory
services.AddKyrolusAuthUserStore<MyUserStore>(); // your storage, your call
```

Every provider shares one options base, so these work the same everywhere: `Scopes`,
`ClaimMappings`, `AdditionalAuthorizationParameters`, `SaveTokens`, `CallbackPath`,
`BackchannelTimeout`, `SchemeName`, `DisplayName`, `RequireVerifiedEmail`, `AutoCreateUser`,
`DefaultRole`, `LinkToExistingUserByEmail`. Anything a specific handler exposes that the shared
surface does not is still reachable through the second parameter:

```csharp
services.AddKyrolusGitHubAuth(
    options => { options.ClientId = "..."; options.ClientSecret = "..."; },
    github => github.UserEmailsEndpoint = "https://github.contoso.com/api/v3/user/emails");
```

**A missing credential fails at startup, not at first sign-in.** Registering a provider with no
client id throws, unless you set `ThrowIfNotConfigured = false` to register it deliberately
disabled. Injecting `IEnumerable<IKyrolusExternalAuthProvider>` gives you the registered
providers - name, scheme, display name, and whether each is actually configured - so a sign-in
page can render its buttons without hard-coding which providers this deployment enables.

#### The external-login hook

The provider packages know how to talk to Google; they know nothing about where users live.
The seam between the two is `IKyrolusExternalLoginHandler`:

```csharp
public ValueTask<KyrolusExternalLoginResult> HandleAsync(
    KyrolusExternalLoginInfo info,          // normalised: ProviderKey, Email, EmailVerified, ...
    KyrolusExternalLoginOptions options,
    CancellationToken cancellationToken);
```

`KyrolusSous.Auth.Runtime` ships a default built on `IKyrolusAuthUserStore` that resolves the
local account, optionally links it to an existing one by verified email, and optionally
provisions a new one. Register your own to replace that logic entirely.

`LinkToExistingUserByEmail` only ever fires on an email the provider states it has **verified**.
Linking on an unverified address is account takeover: anyone able to register that address at a
lax provider would inherit the local account.

A refused login throws `KyrolusExternalLoginException`, which surfaces through the provider
`OnRemoteFailure` event - the documented place to turn it into a redirect:

```csharp
services.AddKyrolusGoogleAuth(
    options => { /* ... */ },
    google => google.Events.OnRemoteFailure = context =>
    {
        var code = (context.Failure as KyrolusExternalLoginException)?.ErrorCode;
        context.Response.Redirect($"/login?error={code}");
        context.HandleResponse();
        return Task.CompletedTask;
    });
```

Throwing is not stylistic. `RemoteAuthenticationHandler` ignores a failed `AuthenticateResult`
set from its ticket-received event and signs the user in anyway, so a refusal expressed that way
would let a rejected identity straight through.

### Authorization server

```csharp
// 1. The application owns its storage.
services.AddDbContext<AppDbContext>(o => o.UseNpgsql(cs).UseOpenIddict());
services.AddOpenIddict().AddCore(c => c.UseEntityFrameworkCore().UseDbContext<AppDbContext>());

// 2. Kyrolus configures the protocol.
services.AddKyrolusOpenIddictAuthServer(options =>
{
    options.Issuer = "https://auth.contoso.com";
    options.SigningCertificate.FilePath = "/run/secrets/signing.pfx";
    options.SigningCertificate.Password = configuration["Auth:SigningPassword"];
    options.DisableAccessTokenEncryption = true;   // APIs validate the JWT locally
});

// 3. And you get the endpoints for free.
app.MapKyrolusOpenIddictEndpoints();
```

`MapKyrolusOpenIddictEndpoints` maps the token, authorization, userinfo and end-session
endpoints. These four handlers are where most OpenIddict deployments keep their bugs:

- **Claim destinations.** OpenIddict drops any claim with no destination, which is why a
  correctly configured server so often issues tokens that look empty. `KyrolusClaimDestinations`
  applies the conventional mapping - access token always, identity token only under the matching
  scope - and `SetKyrolusDestinations()` stamps a whole principal at once.
- **Re-reading the user on refresh.** The token endpoint reloads the account from the store on
  every authorization-code, refresh-token and device-code redemption. A revoked role or a
  disabled account takes effect at the next refresh, not whenever the last long-lived token
  happens to expire.
- **Local validation.** The server registers OpenIddict validation against itself, so its own
  `[Authorize]` endpoints work. Without it the default scheme points at a handler that was never
  registered, and every authenticated request fails at runtime.

Consent is implicit: a client reaching the authorization endpoint with a signed-in user is
granted the scopes it asked for. That is right for first-party clients. A server federating to
third-party clients should set `MapAuthorizationEndpoint = false` and map its own authorization
endpoint with a consent screen.

#### Configuration is validated at startup

`AddKyrolusOpenIddictAuthServer` refuses to build a server that cannot work, and says why: no
signing key; development keys alongside a real certificate (the generated key would silently
win); a refresh flow with no flow that can issue a refresh token; a refresh token that expires
before the access token; reference tokens with token storage disabled; a relative endpoint path;
an issuer that is not an absolute URI.

Certificates load from a file, a base64 blob, an OS certificate store thumbprint, or an
`X509Certificate2` handed over from a key vault. Key storage flags default per OS -
`MachineKeySet` on Windows, `EphemeralKeySet` elsewhere, because a Linux container has no machine
key store and the failure otherwise reads as "the system cannot find the file specified".

### Resource server

```csharp
services.AddKyrolusOpenIddictApiServer(options =>
{
    options.Issuer = "https://auth.contoso.com";
    options.Audiences.Add("orders-api");
    options.ValidationMode = KyrolusTokenValidationMode.Local;   // or Introspection
});
```

`Local` validates against the published keys of the issuer - fast, but blind to a revocation
until the token expires. `Introspection` asks the authorization server about every token - sees
revocations immediately and works with reference tokens, at the cost of a round trip that
OpenIddict caches.

### Password hashing

`KyrolusPbkdf2PasswordHasher` writes the **same wire format as ASP.NET Core Identity v3**, so an
application migrating off `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Identity` keeps every existing password working,
and one migrating back is not trapped either. Legacy Identity v2 hashes verify too, and report
`SuccessRehashNeeded` so they get upgraded on the next successful sign-in - as does any hash
whose stored parameters are weaker than the current configuration.

Defaults are PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA512 over 210,000 iterations (the OWASP recommendation), and startup
validation refuses anything below 10,000. Swap the whole thing out by registering your own
`IKyrolusPasswordHasher` before `AddKyrolusAuthCore()` - bcrypt, Argon2, or whatever the existing
user table already uses.

The sign-in policy hashes a throwaway value even when the username is unknown. Returning early
there would make the response measurably faster for an unknown user than for a known one, which
turns the token endpoint into a user-enumeration oracle. Brute-force lockout is opt-in: register
an `IKyrolusAuthUserLockoutStore` and failures start being counted.

### Trimming and AOT

Every package here builds with `IsAotCompatible` and no trim or AOT analyzer warnings. That
includes the mapped endpoints, which use `RequestDelegate` rather than the reflective
`Map*(..., Delegate)` overloads, and the userinfo response, which is written with
`Utf8JsonWriter` instead of a serializer. The guarantee covers this code; whether a full
`PublishAot` succeeds also depends on OpenIddict and the provider handlers, which have their own
trimming characteristics.

## KyrolusSous.Mapping (Abstractions + Runtime + Generator)

A high-performance, enterprise-grade, **Zero-Dependency**, **100% Native AOT & Trimming Compliant** object-to-object mapping and LINQ projection ecosystem for .NET 10 & .NET Standard 2.0.

### Key Architecture Highlights
- **Zero Third-Party Dependencies**: Pure .NET with 0 external libraries (no AutoMapper, no Mapster, no dynamic Emit).
- **Compile-Time Source Generator (`KyrolusSous.Mapping.Generator`)**: Generates direct property assignment C# code at compile-time with 0 allocations, 0 reflection, and 0 runtime overhead.
- **Compiled Expression Runtime (`KyrolusSous.Mapping.Runtime`)**: High-throughput expression-compiled engine supporting deep object graphs, pre-allocated collections, flattening, and circular reference safety.
- **Database Query Projections (`ProjectTo`)**: Compiles LINQ expression trees directly into EF Core SQL `SELECT` statements for maximum database query performance.
- **HTTP PATCH / Ignore Null Semantics**: Effortless in-place entity updates preserving existing database values.

---

### Attribute Compatibility Matrix

The following table details which attributes are consumed by the **Roslyn Source Generator**, the **Runtime Engine**, or **EF Core Projections**:

| Attribute | Target | Generator | Runtime | EF Projections | Description & Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :---: | :---: | :---: | :--- |
| **`[KyrolusMapTo(Type, IsBidirectional)]`** | Class, Struct, Interface | ✅ | ✅ | ➖ | Instructs mapping from the decorated source type to the specified target type. When `IsBidirectional = true`, generates both directions. |
| **`[KyrolusMapFrom(Type, IsBidirectional)]`** | Class, Struct, Interface | ✅ | ✅ | ➖ | Instructs mapping from the specified source type into the decorated destination type. |
| **`[KyrolusMapper]`** | Partial Class | ✅ | ➖ | ➖ | **Generator Only:** Marks a `partial class` for compile-time generation of `partial` mapping methods. |
| **`[KyrolusIgnoreMap]`** | Property, Field, Parameter | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Skips the member entirely during mapping and projection operations (e.g., password hashes, internal tokens). |
| **`[KyrolusMapProperty("SourceName")]`** | Property, Field, Parameter | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | Maps a property to a differently named source/destination property. |
| **`[KyrolusIgnoreNull]`** | Class, Struct, Property | ✅ | ✅ | ➖ | **HTTP PATCH:** When mapping in-place, source properties with `null` values will NOT overwrite existing target values. |
| **`[KyrolusMapConstructor]`** | Constructor | ➖ | ✅ | ➖ | **Runtime Only:** Selects a specific constructor overload to instantiate the target type when multiple constructors exist. |
| **`[KyrolusUseConverter(Type)]`** | Class, Struct, Property | ➖ | ✅ | ➖ | **Runtime Only:** Uses a custom `IKyrolusTypeConverter` or `IKyrolusValueResolver` for specialized transformations. |

---

### Comprehensive Usage Examples

#### 1. Compile-Time Source Generation (Zero Runtime / Pure AOT)

##### A. Direct Extension Methods (`[KyrolusMapTo]` / `[KyrolusMapFrom]`)
```csharp
using KyrolusSous.Mapping.Abstractions.Attributes;
using KyrolusSous.Mapping.Generated;

// Decorate your entity or DTO:
[KyrolusMapTo(typeof(CustomerDto), IsBidirectional = true)]
public class Customer
{
    public Guid Id { get; set; }
    public string FullName { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    public decimal Balance { get; set; }
    
    [KyrolusIgnoreMap]
    public string InternalNotes { get; set; } = string.Empty;
}

public class CustomerDto
{
    public Guid Id { get; set; }
    public string FullName { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    public decimal Balance { get; set; }
}

// Usage in your code (pure compile-time extension method, 0 reflection):
var customer = new Customer { Id = Guid.NewGuid(), FullName = "Kyrolus Sous", Balance = 5000m };
CustomerDto dto = customer.ToCustomerDto();

// Bidirectional reverse mapping:
Customer restored = dto.ToCustomer();
```

##### B. Compile-Time Partial Mappers (`[KyrolusMapper]`)
```csharp
[KyrolusMapper]
public static partial class UserMapper
{
    // The source generator automatically generates the implementation at compile-time:
    public static partial UserDto MapToDto(User user);
    public static partial void MapInPlace(UpdateUserDto dto, User entity);
}

// Usage:
UserDto dto = UserMapper.MapToDto(user);
UserMapper.MapInPlace(updateDto, userEntity);
```

##### C. Positional Records & Primary Constructors
```csharp
public class ProductEntity
{
    public int Id { get; set; }
    public string Title { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    public decimal Price { get; set; }
}

[KyrolusMapFrom(typeof(ProductEntity))]
public record ProductDto(int Id, string Title, decimal Price);

// Generated code invokes the record's primary constructor:
var dto = productEntity.ToProductDto();
```

---

#### 2. Runtime & Dependency Injection Mapping (`IKyrolusObjectMapper`)

##### A. DI Registration (`Program.cs`)
```csharp
builder.Services.AddKyrolusMapping(config =>
{
    config.EnableFlattening = true;
    config.EnableCircularReferenceTracking = true;
    config.AddProfile<CatalogMappingProfile>();
});
```

##### B. Basic Mapping & Deep Cloning
```csharp
public class OrderService(IKyrolusObjectMapper mapper)
{
    public OrderResponseDto CreateOrder(OrderEntity order)
    {
        // 1. Map Entity to DTO
        OrderResponseDto dto = mapper.Map<OrderEntity, OrderResponseDto>(order);

        // 2. Create Deep Clone of an entire object graph safely
        OrderEntity orderCopy = mapper.Clone(order);

        return dto;
    }
}
```

##### C. HTTP PATCH / In-Place Mapping (`[KyrolusIgnoreNull]` / `.IgnoreNullValues()`)
```csharp
// Existing entity in DbContext:
var entity = await dbContext.Users.FindAsync(userId);

// Incoming PATCH request with partial fields:
var patchDto = new UpdateUserRequest { Email = "new@example.com", Name = null };

// Mutates entity in-place without overwriting Name with null:
mapper.Map(patchDto, entity);

await dbContext.SaveChangesAsync();
```

##### D. Circular Reference Safety (`KyrolusMappingContext`)
```csharp
public class Category
{
    public int Id { get; set; }
    public string Name { get; set; } = string.Empty;
    public List<Product> Products { get; set; } = [];
}

public class Product
{
    public int Id { get; set; }
    public Category Category { get; set; } = null!;
}

// Circular graphs (Category -> Product -> Category) map without StackOverflowException:
var dto = mapper.Map<Category, CategoryDto>(category);
```

---

#### 3. Fluent Mapping Profiles (`KyrolusMappingProfile`)

```csharp
public class CatalogMappingProfile : KyrolusMappingProfile
{
    public CatalogMappingProfile()
    {
        CreateMap<Product, ProductDto>()
            .ForMember(dest => dest.FormattedPrice, opt => opt.MapFrom(src => $"${src.Price:F2}"))
            .ForMember(dest => dest.Badge, opt => opt.UseValue("Featured"))
            // Conditional Mapping: only map discount when product has promotion active
            .ForMember(dest => dest.SpecialDiscount, opt => opt.Condition(src => src.HasPromotion))
            .BeforeMap((src, dest, ctx) => Console.WriteLine("Starting product mapping..."))
            .AfterMap((src, dest, ctx) => dest.LastSyncedUtc = DateTime.UtcNow)
            .Ignore(dest => dest.InternalCost)
            .IgnoreNullValues()
            .ReverseMap();

        CreateMap<Money, decimal>()
            .ConvertUsing(src => src.Amount);
    }
}
```

##### Self-Diagnostic Validation (`AssertConfigurationIsValid`)
Run automated self-tests to ensure all registered profiles and entity-to-DTO mappings are 100% valid and have no unmapped fields:
```csharp
var config = new KyrolusMappingConfiguration();
config.AddProfile<CatalogMappingProfile>();

// Validates mappings and throws KyrolusMappingValidationException if unmapped properties exist
config.AssertConfigurationIsValid();
```

---

#### 4. EF Core Database Query Projections (`ProjectTo`)

```csharp
// Optimized SQL SELECT projection: only required columns are queried from the database:
public async Task<List<ProductSummaryDto>> GetCatalogAsync(AppDbContext dbContext, IKyrolusObjectMapper mapper)
{
    return await dbContext.Products
        .Where(p => p.IsActive)
        .ProjectTo<ProductEntity, ProductSummaryDto>(mapper)
        .ToListAsync();
}
```
